disease_label_per_paper: Profound hypernatremia in the setting of hyperosmotic hyperglycemic state
presentation_summary: 50-year-old otherwise healthy woman was brought to the emergency department for confusion after progressive lethargy, confusion, and altered gait.
On presentation, glucose was approximately 1400 mg/dL and sodium was 169 mmol/L; the corrected sodium was reported as greater than 200 mmol/L.
The case report states her total serum osmolality was 437 mOsm/kg, with anion gap and serum bicarbonate within normal limits and no metabolic acidosis or ketosis.
HbA1c was greater than 14, indicating previously unrecognized diabetes.
She had a 14 L free-water deficit and prerenal AKI; creatinine was 2.22 mg/dL from a baseline of 0.5 mg/dL.
The course was complicated by rhabdomyolysis with peak CK 2493 U/L, UTI/septic shock trigger context, aspiration pneumonia, and later MRI evidence of an acute right caudate infarct.

quality_warnings: Culture species, UTI source attribution, aspiration pneumonia, septic shock treatment, and final stroke workup are confirmatory/non-ranking context unless explicitly testing a post-workup mode.

The case report abstract mentions plasma osmolality 340 mOsm/kg, while the case presentation and discussion report total serum osmolality 437 mOsm/kg; the case-presentation value is used for the rankable snapshot.
Normal anion gap and bicarbonate are encoded with normal_flag_only rather than invented numeric values.
Stroke and rhabdomyolysis are preserved as non-ranking course/confirmatory event context because they were identified after the presentation snapshot.
